name: Poor Law Unions 5 Apr 1891
description: The 160 Poor Law Unions of Ireland at the census of 5 Apr 1891, as Table VI of each 1891 county report lists them. The same unions stood from the dissolution of Gortin on 1 Apr 1889 until Glin was dissolved on 30 Sep 1891. Each union is drawn as the 1907-12 District Electoral Divisions (Phelim Birch's and Paddy Matthews's maps) that cover its 1891 divisions, matched by name from hand transcriptions of the printed tables (Mayo and Sligo from OCR, checked by hand). Each union carries its land area (land_acres: the map area less large lakes and tideway, which the census also leaves out), the sum of its printed county-part acreages (census_acres), the difference (pct_diff) and a confidence grade. Of the 152 unions that can be checked, 148 agree within 1% (134 within 0.5%; median 0.09%); Belfast (+6.7%, reclaimed foreshore inside the later city wards), Wexford (+4.8%, reclaimed slobs), Donegal (-3.0%, Lough Eask counted by the census) and Glenties (+1.8%) are further out. Eight unions are graded unchecked: the five with King's County parts (Parsonstown, Tullamore, Edenderry, Roscrea and Mountmellick), whose King's County divisions are approximated because no King's County report is held: each union is grown from its workhouse town and original divisions towards the King's County area implied by the 1911 General Report Table 51 (against those areas Parsonstown is +1.7%, Tullamore +1.0%, Roscrea +3.4%, Edenderry -4.9% and Mountmellick -12.7%); and Abbeyleix, Athy and Carlow, whose Queen's County parts follow the 1911 Queen's County table because the 1891 report is not held. Carlow is unresolved: its 1891 Carlow part (148,021 acres) and its Queen's County part come to about 185,100 acres, but Table 51 gives 199,998 in 1911. The map is simplified for display by a coverage simplification of the division map, so neighbouring unions keep common edges (95% of divisions lie within 10 m of the full lines); the full-resolution file is among the downloads.
